en.title: Ebon Moss-Bachrach on 'The Bear' Role: 'You Have to Be a Perennial!'
en.summary: The Bear's Richie Jerimovich, **Ebon Moss-Bachrach**, offers a profound piece of advice for enduring in the entertainment industry. His perspective on longevity and adaptability resonates deeply with fans invested in the demanding world of television.
en.body:
In the high-pressure, ever-shifting world of television acting, maintaining a career requires more than just talent; it demands a specific kind of resilience. **Ebon Moss-Bachrach**, the actor behind the fan-favorite character Richie Jerimovich in FX's critically acclaimed series **The Bear**, recently shared a key insight into what it takes to thrive in the industry. His advice is simple yet profound, emphasizing the importance of continuous growth and adaptability for anyone working in creative fields.

"You have to be a perennial! It's very important when you work as an actor, or in any," Moss-Bachrach stated, highlighting a mindset that encourages constant learning and reinvention. This "perennial" approach suggests a need to remain relevant, like a plant that blooms year after year, by consistently adapting to new challenges and opportunities. For fans of **The Bear**, this statement offers a fascinating glimpse into the actor's own professional philosophy, which likely informs his nuanced portrayal of Richie's own journey of self-discovery and professional redemption throughout the series' two seasons. Richie's arc, from a disgruntled, seemingly stagnant figure to someone actively seeking purpose and improvement, mirrors this idea of being a "perennial" in his own right.

## The 'Perennial' Actor in Action

This philosophy is particularly resonant for viewers who have watched Richie's dramatic transformation. **The Bear** has masterfully depicted the struggles and triumphs of its characters, and Richie's storyline has been a central pillar of that success. His journey has involved confronting his own shortcomings, embracing new responsibilities, and finding a sense of pride in his work, even when it's difficult. Moss-Bachrach's "perennial" outlook suggests that this kind of growth isn't just good storytelling; it's a necessary survival strategy for actors navigating the unpredictable nature of Hollywood. The ability to adapt to new roles, evolving industry demands, and the inherent insecurities of the profession is what separates those who have fleeting moments of fame from those who build lasting careers. Fans connect with these characters because their struggles often mirror real-world challenges, and Richie's path towards becoming a "perennial" offers a hopeful, inspiring narrative.

## What This Means for **The Bear** Fans

For the passionate fanbase of **The Bear**, Moss-Bachrach's quote adds another layer of appreciation for the show's commitment to character development. It underscores the idea that the actors, much like the characters they play, must also be "perennials" in their craft. This perspective might lead viewers to look closer at the subtle choices Moss-Bachrach makes in his performance, understanding that his portrayal is informed by a deep understanding of sustained professional effort. As the series continues, this "perennial" mindset will undoubtedly be crucial for Richie's continued evolution, as well as for the entire ensemble cast as they navigate the future of the restaurant and their personal lives. It’s a reminder that great characters, like great careers, are cultivated over time with persistent effort and a willingness to change.

## What's Next

While the exact release date for **The Bear** Season 3 has not yet been announced, fans can anticipate more of the intense character studies and culinary drama that has defined the series. Ebon Moss-Bachrach is expected to return as Richie Jerimovich, continuing his compelling journey.

content_raw: The Bear star Ebon Moss-Bachrach shares some food for thought when it comes to finding inspiration at work.
